projects.name: XOFram
projects.problem: A third-party agriculture template shipped as static HTML, CSS and jQuery. The same markup was duplicated across five pages, so any change had to be made five times.
projects.approach: Rebuilt it as a React component tree. Moved the page content into a single data module so sections render from data instead of repeated markup, and replaced hash links with real routes.
projects.stack: React 18, React Router 6, Tailwind CSS 3, Swiper
projects.outcome: Five routed pages from one shared component set. Changing a section is now one edit in one file.
projects.honesty: A rebuild of a template I did not design. The work here is the architecture, not the visual design.

projects.name: Netflix Clone
projects.problem: I wanted to find out what changes when an interface is driven entirely by a live API instead of fixed content.
projects.approach: Built a catalogue on TheMovieDB with category browsing, search and lazy-loaded artwork. State lives in Pinia so every view reads one source of truth. The app picks up the browser language and falls back to English when the API has no match for it.
projects.stack: Vue 3, Pinia, Vue Router, Swiper, TheMovieDB API
projects.outcome: The language fallback is the part I still reuse. It is the same problem this site solves in Turkish and English.
projects.honesty: Built to learn the stack. The interface follows Netflix's.

projects.name: Agentic Starter Kit
projects.problem: Every AI coding tool reads its own instruction file. Keeping eight of them in agreement by hand meant they drifted apart within a week.
projects.approach: One canonical AGENTS.md holds the rules. The client-specific files for Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, Aider and Junie are thin pointers back to it, so there is one place to edit.
projects.outcome: Starting a project means copying one folder instead of writing eight instruction files.
projects.honesty: A working convention, not an application.

about.label: Approach
body: I am a frontend developer at InspireIT in Ankara. Alongside it I am finishing a management information systems degree at İstanbul University.

Most of what I do is the unglamorous half of frontend: taking something that already works and making it easier to change. Splitting a page into parts that stand on their own. Removing what is on screen until what matters is obvious.
I am early in this. Everything listed here is work I actually did, described as it is.
